<a id="T008"></a>
## T008

- Date: 1963-09-14
- Place: Tokyo, Japan
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Convention on Offences and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft was concluded.

Summary: On 14 September 1963, the Convention on Offences and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft was concluded in Tokyo. It covers acts affecting in-flight safety, lets the aircraft commander restrain a suspected offender, and requires States to take custody of offenders, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism. The UN lists it as the first of the international legal instruments against terrorism.

Citation: [CONV-TOKYO1963](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-TOKYO1963) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv1-english.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv1-english.pdf))

<a id="T009"></a>
## T009

- Date: 1970-12-16
- Place: The Hague, Netherlands
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft was concluded.

Summary: On 16 December 1970, the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft was concluded in The Hague. It makes seizing control of an aircraft in flight by force or threat an offence, requires severe penalties, and obliges States holding an offender to extradite or prosecute, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism.

Citation: [CONV-HAGUE1970](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-HAGUE1970) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv2-english.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv2-english.pdf))

<a id="T010"></a>
## T010

- Date: 1971-09-23
- Place: Montreal, Canada
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation was concluded.

Summary: On 23 September 1971, the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation was concluded in Montreal. It makes violence that endangers an aircraft in flight, and placing explosive devices on aircraft, offences that States must punish or extradite for, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism. A 1988 protocol later extended it to airports (T023).

Citation: [CONV-MONTREAL1971](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-MONTREAL1971) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv3-english.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv3-english.pdf))

<a id="T011"></a>
## T011

- Date: 1972-12-18
- Place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 3034 (XXVII) on measures to prevent international terrorism.

Summary: On 18 December 1972, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution 3034 (XXVII) on measures to prevent international terrorism. The resolution set up a 35-member Ad Hoc Committee on International Terrorism. It is the earliest General Assembly action on terrorism recorded in CTA6.

Citation: [UNGA3034](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNGA3034) ([https://undocs.org/A/RES/3034\(XXVII\)](https://undocs.org/A/RES/3034(XXVII)))

<a id="T012"></a>
## T012

- Date: 1973-07-25
- Place: United Kingdom (Northern Ireland)
- Region: Europe
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UK Parliament enacted the Northern Ireland (Emergency Provisions) Act 1973.

Summary: On 25 July 1973, the UK Parliament enacted the Northern Ireland (Emergency Provisions) Act 1973. It covers the trial and punishment of certain offences and offences against public security and order in Northern Ireland. It is one of the emergency laws later examined by the European Court of Human Rights (for example T016 and T025).

Citation: [UK-NIEPA1973](../sources/regions/europe.md#UK-NIEPA1973) ([https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1973/53/contents](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1973/53/contents))

<a id="T013"></a>
## T013

- Date: 1973-12-14
- Place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Crimes against Internationally Protected Persons was adopted.

Summary: On 14 December 1973, the UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Crimes against Internationally Protected Persons, including Diplomatic Agents. It requires States to criminalize murder, kidnapping and other attacks on heads of State, foreign ministers and officials entitled to special protection abroad, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism. The UN Treaty Collection holds it as a deposited treaty.

Citations:

- [CONV-IPP1973](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-IPP1973) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/english-18-7.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/english-18-7.pdf))
- [UNTC-XVIII](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNTC-XVIII) ([https://treaties.un.org/Pages/Treaties.aspx?id=18&subid=A&clang=_en](https://treaties.un.org/Pages/Treaties.aspx?id=18&subid=A&clang=_en))

<a id="T014"></a>
## T014

- Date: 1974-11-29
- Place: London, United Kingdom
- Region: Europe
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1974.

Summary: On 29 November 1974, the UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1974. It provided for proscribed organisations, exclusion orders, and powers of detention and prosecution, as a temporary measure. It was followed by the 1989 Act (T027) and, eventually, the Terrorism Act 2000 (T049).

Citation: [UK-PTA1974](../sources/regions/europe.md#UK-PTA1974) ([https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/56/contents](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/56/contents))

## T016

- Date: 1978-01-18
- Place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
- Region: Europe
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in Ireland v. the United Kingdom.

Summary: On 18 January 1978, the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in Ireland v. the United Kingdom, an inter-State case. According to the Court's factsheet, it concerned UK internment and five interrogation techniques used in Northern Ireland from 1971 to 1975, and the Court found a violation of Article 3 (inhuman and degrading treatment).

Citation: [ECHR-IRELAND1978](../sources/regions/europe.md#ECHR-IRELAND1978) ([https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-57506](https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-57506))

<a id="T017"></a>
## T017

- Date: 1978-09-06
- Place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
- Region: Europe
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in K. and Others v. Germany (no. 5029/71) on secret surveillance legislation.

Summary: On 6 September 1978, the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in K. and Others v. Germany (no. 5029/71) on secret surveillance legislation. According to the Court's factsheet, the Court found no violation of Article 8, accepting that, under exceptional conditions, secret surveillance powers could be necessary because of the threat of espionage and terrorism.

Citation: [ECHR-1978-5029](../sources/regions/europe.md#ECHR-1978-5029) ([https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-57510](https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-57510))

## T018

- Date: 1979-12-17
- Place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The International Convention against the Taking of Hostages was adopted.

Summary: On 17 December 1979, the UN General Assembly adopted the International Convention against the Taking of Hostages. It defines hostage-taking as seizing or detaining a person and threatening them to compel a State, organization or other third party to act or refrain from acting, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism.

Citations:

- [CONV-HOSTAGES1979](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-HOSTAGES1979) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/english-18-5.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/english-18-5.pdf))
- [UNTC-XVIII](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNTC-XVIII) ([https://treaties.un.org/Pages/Treaties.aspx?id=18&subid=A&clang=_en](https://treaties.un.org/Pages/Treaties.aspx?id=18&subid=A&clang=_en))

<a id="T019"></a>
## T019

- Date: 1980-03-03
- Place: Vienna, Austria and New York, United States
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material was opened for signature.

Summary: On 3 March 1980, the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material was opened for signature in Vienna and New York. It criminalizes the unlawful possession, use, transfer or theft of nuclear material and threats to use it, according to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, and was amended in 2005 to cover nuclear facilities and domestic use, storage and transport.

Citation: [CONV-NUCMAT1980](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-NUCMAT1980) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv6-english.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv6-english.pdf))

## T020

- Date: 1985-12-09
- Place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 40/61 on measures to prevent international terrorism.

Summary: On 9 December 1985, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution 40/61 on measures to prevent international terrorism. It calls on all States not to organize, instigate, assist or participate in terrorist acts in other States, or to allow such activities on their territory, and to implement the Ad Hoc Committee's recommendations.

Citation: [UNGA40-61](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNGA40-61) ([https://undocs.org/A/RES/40/61](https://undocs.org/A/RES/40/61))

## T021

- Date: 1985-12-18
- Place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN Security Council adopted resolution 579 (1985) on hostage-taking and abduction.

Summary: On 18 December 1985, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 579 on hostage-taking and abduction, condemning unequivocally all such acts. It is among the Council's earliest resolutions on terrorism-related acts recorded in CTA6.

Citation: [UNSC579](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNSC579) ([https://undocs.org/S/RES/579\(1985\)](https://undocs.org/S/RES/579(1985)))

France enacted Loi n° 86-1020 relative à la lutte contre le terrorisme.

## T023

- Date: 1988-02-24
- Place: Montreal, Canada
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts of Violence at Airports Serving International Civil Aviation was concluded.

Summary: On 24 February 1988, the Protocol for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts of Violence at Airports Serving International Civil Aviation was concluded in Montreal. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it extends the 1971 Montreal Convention (T010) to terrorist acts at airports serving international civil aviation.

Citation: [CONV-AIRPORTS1988](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-AIRPORTS1988) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv7-english.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv7-english.pdf))

<a id="T024"></a>
## T024

- Date: 1988-03-10
- Place: Rome, Italy
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Maritime Navigation was concluded.

Summary: On 10 March 1988, the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Maritime Navigation was concluded in Rome. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it applies to shipping a legal regime similar to the aviation conventions, making it an offence to seize a ship by force or endanger its safe navigation.

Citation: [CONV-SUA1988](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-SUA1988) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv8-english.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv8-english.pdf))

## T025

- Date: 1988-11-29
- Place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
- Region: Europe
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in B. and Others v. the United Kingdom (nos. 11209/84 and others) concerning detention under prevention-of-terrorism legislation.

Summary: On 29 November 1988, the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in B. and Others v. the United Kingdom (nos. 11209/84 and others), on detention under prevention-of-terrorism legislation in Northern Ireland. According to the Court's factsheet, it found a violation of Article 5 § 3 because holding suspects for four days and six hours or more before bringing them before a judge was not 'prompt'.

Citation: [ECHR-1988-11209](../sources/regions/europe.md#ECHR-1988-11209) ([https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-57450](https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-57450))

<a id="T026"></a>
## T026

- Date: 1988-12-21
- Place: Lockerbie, Scotland, United Kingdom
- Region: Europe
- Theme: major operations
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

Pan Am Flight 103 was destroyed by a bomb over Lockerbie, according to the FBI's history page.

Summary: On 21 December 1988, Pan Am Flight 103 was destroyed by a bomb over Lockerbie, Scotland, according to the FBI's history page. The FBI says all 259 people on board and 11 people on the ground were killed, and describes it as one of the world's most lethal acts of air terrorism before 9/11. The UN Security Council later addressed it in resolution 731 (1992).

Citation: [FBI-PANAM103](../sources/regions/europe.md#FBI-PANAM103) ([https://www.fbi.gov/history/famous-cases/pan-am-103-bombing](https://www.fbi.gov/history/famous-cases/pan-am-103-bombing))

## T027

- Date: 1989-03-15
- Place: London, United Kingdom
- Region: Europe
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1989.

Summary: On 15 March 1989, the UK Parliament enacted the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act 1989. It covered proscription, exclusion, financial assistance for terrorism, and powers of arrest, stop and search and detention. It continued the temporary-provisions model of the 1974 Act (T014) until the Terrorism Act 2000 (T049).

Citation: [UK-PTA1989](../sources/regions/europe.md#UK-PTA1989) ([https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1989/4/contents](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1989/4/contents))

- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN Security Council adopted resolution 635 (1989) on marking plastic or sheet explosives for detection.

Summary: On 14 June 1989, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 635 on marking plastic or sheet explosives so they can be detected. The Council condemned unlawful interference with civil aviation and called on States to cooperate in preventing terrorism involving explosives. A convention on marking plastic explosives followed in 1991 (T030).

Citation: [UNSC635](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNSC635) ([https://undocs.org/S/RES/635\(1989\)](https://undocs.org/S/RES/635(1989)))

A chapter on terrorism (Article 139) was added to Mexico's Federal Penal Code (amendment published in the DOF on 29 July 1970, per the consolidated code).
